label: prop:brane-boundary
title: Structure of the defining boundary
html:
The defining boundary \partial A_n (brane boundary) possesses four key properties:

  1. Codimension. In the archimedean realisation, \partial A_n corresponds to a closed subset in \mathcal{S}_n of real codimension
  \mathrm{codim}_{\mathbb{R}}\!\left(\partial A_n \subset \mathcal{S}_n\right) \geq 2.
  1. Exceptional object. At each degeneration locus of the restriction r_n, the kernel \ker(r_n|_S) is isomorphic to a simple object of \mathbf{C}. Archimedianly, this is \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2, the exceptional divisor of the topological blow-up.
  2. Involution symmetry. The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) restricts to an endomorphism of \partial A_n. Its fixed subobjects coincide with the monodromy fixed points of the quantum characteristic classes.
  3. Chirality interface (archimedean). When n = 1, \partial \mathcal{S}_1 isolates macroscopic spacetime from internal chiral modes. It forms the geometric boundary separating the base M from the gauge fibre, across which the Reeb involution \xi \mapsto -\xi (Descartes chirality) reverses orientation.
